findings.description: The token horizon divides total watchdog time by configured concurrency even when the plan cannot achieve that parallelism. For one a1_full build trial with watchdog_s=16800 and --concurrency 9, the required horizon is only 62 minutes, although that trial's phase budgets total 140 minutes. A token expiring in 90 minutes passes preflight.
findings.failure_mode: The accepted token can expire during an otherwise valid trial. Since pipeline-run.sh replaces its refresh token with a placeholder, later Codex calls cannot authenticate or renew it, degrading the evaluation.
findings.suggested_fix: Calculate a conservative scheduling horizon that accounts for available trials and scheduling tails, including retries. At minimum, the horizon must cover the longest individual trial regardless of configured concurrency.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: The reserved set is built from every .py basename (overlay: all .py; fixture: all .py under any tests/ or test/ component), but pytest's basename-collision failure only exists for modules pytest itself imports by basename: files matching python_files (default test_*.py, *_test.py) and conftest.py. Helper modules such as tests/helpers.py, tests/utils.py, tests/common.py, tests/_oracle_x.py or data files under tests/fixtures/ never produce 'import file mismatch', yet their names are reserved, and the tree walk visits every directory (src/, app/, vendor/, an agent-created .venv/ or node_modules/). An agent that adds app/helpers.py or pkg/utils.py (extremely common names) while the fixture has tests/helpers.py has its source module silently deleted before the test command runs. This sharpens the primary reviewer's concern 1 with the actual pytest rule and a fix.
findings.failure_mode: A correct solution whose new source module shares a basename with any non-test helper or data .py under the fixture's tests/ is deleted from the grading tree; hidden tests ImportError and the row records a failing solution (counted as a 'collision' in grade.json, so the cause is invisible in the pass/fail metric).
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict reserved to names pytest collects: fnmatch against test_*.py / *_test.py (or read python_files from pytest.ini/pyproject/setup.cfg in the fixture) and never reserve helper/data modules. Consider restricting the removal walk to directories the test_command collects, and skip .venv/, node_modules/, .git/ and other hidden dirs.

findings.description: The codex CLI's API-key login writes auth.json as {"OPENAI_API_KEY": "sk-...", "tokens": null, "last_refresh": null}. The pre-flight treats a null tokens object as 'has no tokens.access_token' and refuses every non-smoke batch (fresh, --resume and --dry-run) with the instruction 'run codex login on the host', which cannot change anything for an API-key host. pipeline-run.sh would have copied such a file verbatim (tokens is not a dict, so nothing is rewritten) and codex would work. The refusal is per the new header spec, but the spec itself breaks a valid credential mode and KF-048 (single-use refresh token) does not apply to API keys at all.
findings.failure_mode: Hosts using codex with an API key cannot start any non-smoke ablation batch; the refusal message points at a login that does not fix it.
findings.suggested_fix: When tokens is null/absent and OPENAI_API_KEY is a non-empty string, treat the file as checked=false with a WARN (no expiry to verify) instead of refusing; only refuse when neither an API key nor a decodable access token is present.

findings.description: required_until = now + 2 x sum(watchdog_s) / concurrency, where watchdog_s is already 2 x the phase-sum budget. For the full suite v2 plan (12 build tasks x 3 trials x 7 codex arms at ~15000-16800 s watchdog each, plus 84 review-catch trials at 7200 s) the horizon is roughly 2.9 million seconds at concurrency 3, i.e. on the order of a month. A ChatGPT-mode codex access token (JWT exp) does not live that long after a fresh login, so a full batch is refused unconditionally and the message 'run codex login on the host' cannot satisfy the check. Even mid-size batches are refused when a fresh token would in practice outlive the realistic runtime by a wide margin.
findings.failure_mode: The pre-flight makes the batch sizes the runner exists for unrunnable regardless of operator action; operators will work around it with --smoke or by editing the plan, defeating the KF-048 protection.
findings.suggested_fix: Base the horizon on an expected duration (sum of phase_sum_min / concurrency, or est from prior rows), or compare the token to a configurable horizon and downgrade an exceeded horizon to a WARN recorded in codex_preflight plus a per-trial check in pipeline-run.sh before each codex-using phase.

findings.description: COLLIDING[0] is incremented on every prepare() call in a grade, and remove_colliding writes a <tree>.colliding-removed.txt sidecar for every prepared tree even when nothing was found. If prepare runs for more than the final tree (reference/self-check tree, took_effect snapshot trees), grade.json colliding_tests_removed is the sum over all of them rather than 'agent files removed from the graded tree', and extra empty sidecars appear beside each tree. The docstring and AG-35 only cover the single-tree case.
findings.failure_mode: Telemetry over-counts collisions when several trees are prepared; empty sidecar files accumulate next to every prepared tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the count and let the caller attribute it to the final tree only; write the sidecar only when found is non-empty or only for the final label.

findings.cross_file_justification: The suite comment says reserve_usd 'is kept for spend.sh' and that a batch's --max-usd is 1,500 - spend - concurrency x the largest cap; spend.sh is not in the diff and still reads caps.run_usd (12), which is now only the fallback while the effective caps are 15 and 20.
findings.description: run_usd stays 12 as the single-cap fallback while the effective per-kind caps become 15 (build) and 20 (review-catch). Any consumer outside run-ablation.sh that derives the concurrency reservation or the recommended --max-usd from caps.run_usd (spend.sh per the suite comment, and the manifest reader for older tooling) now under-reserves by concurrency x 8 USD and can recommend a --max-usd that lets the cycle cap be exceeded.
findings.failure_mode: The cycle budget guard computed from caps.run_usd is 8 USD per in-flight trial too generous; a batch sized from that figure can overspend the 1,500 USD cycle cap.
findings.suggested_fix: Have spend.sh (and any other reader) take max(run_usd_by_type[*]) when present, falling back to run_usd; or set run_usd to the largest per-kind cap so single-cap readers stay conservative.
